name: High-effort / low-effort post tags

card.summary: Title tags on looksmaxxing forums that mark long, researched guides as 'high effort' and throwaway posts as 'no value', helping readers find the detailed looks-improvement guides worth reading.
card.aka: high effort post, no value post
card.note: Tags are self-applied by posters; they signal intent, not accuracy.

quick.overview:
On forums such as looksmax.org, thread titles are often prefixed with '[High effort]' or 'high effort'. The tag tells readers the author spent time researching and writing a detailed guide, for example on physique, skincare, photos or pharmacology. A matching 'no value post' prefix is used for short, casual threads that the author does not expect to contain useful information.

For people trying to improve their appearance, the tags work as a rough filter. Long guides on topics such as upper-body training, grooming or dating-profile photos are easier to find when marked, and casual updates are labelled so they do not get mistaken for advice. The tags are applied by the posters themselves.
quick.how: A poster types the tag at the start of a thread title, then writes a long structured post, often with sections and a conclusion. Readers search for or scroll for the tag to find guides. Casual posts use 'no value post' in the same position, often as a self-deprecating joke.
quick.risks: Because anyone can add the tag, it describes the author's effort rather than the correctness of the content. Several tagged threads cover medical or pharmacological topics, and readers rely on the usual caution about forum health information.

lead: High-effort and low-effort post tags are informal title prefixes used on looksmaxxing forums, most visibly looksmax.org. A thread starting with 'high effort' signals a long, researched guide, while a thread starting with 'no value post' signals a short or casual contribution.[1][2]

The tags help members find detailed guides on ways to improve appearance. Threads carrying the high-effort tag in the community cover subjects such as physique training, softmaxxing, photo selection and the 'pill' framework of beliefs, each presented as a comprehensive write-up.[1][3] Casual threads such as a post about a supplement arriving by mail are labelled 'no value post' by their authors.[4]

The tags are a community convention, not a formal feature. No published research has examined them, although academic literature on the effort-reward balance in work and on 'learned industriousness' studies how effort is valued more broadly.[5][6]

chain: Poster tags a thread as high effort or no value
Easier to find thorough advice on grooming, physique and style
angle.text: The tags do not change appearance themselves. They steer readers toward long, structured guides on looks topics and mark casual chatter, which shortens the search for detailed material.

infobox: high effort, [High effort], no value post
Signal length and effort of a post

paras: A 'high effort' tag is placed in the title, usually at the start, and sometimes in square brackets. Threads using it on looksmax.org include a full 'pill spectrum' write-up, a guide to upper-body development, a Tinder pictures guide, a prettyboy softmaxxing guide, a fitness-styles tier list and a guide to moles.[1][7][8]
The counterpart 'no value post' is used for brief personal updates, such as a note about a received supplement or a remark about mewing and tongue strength.[4][9]

Members use the tag as shorthand for the culture's expectation that real guides be sourced and structured. Authors often add the tag to threads on topics where members want detail, such as training or hormone-related topics. The tag also shows up in 'megaguide'-style titles.

No studies found. Related academic work on effort and reward includes a review of the effort-reward imbalance model in occupational health and a psychology review on learned industriousness, neither of which concerns forum tags.[5][6]
